Two kraals in Masikili had respectively eight and six cattle that showed suspicious recovering FMD mouth lesions. One of these kraals was also infected in the last outbreak in 2011. Masikili area was vaccinated for FMD in February 2013 and again in June 2013.
One kraal of 156 cattle was inspected whereby two had fresh ulcers on their tongues and 11 had old healing ulcerative lesions. This kraal was last vaccinated for FMD in March 2013.

The total cattle population on Ivilivinzi Village is 761 consisting of all age groups and sexes that are farmed under communal farming systems. The breed of cattle is predominantly the Sanga.During the second surveillance investigation, further seven suspicious cattle were sampled from one of the two kraals where the first suspected outbreak was reported in Ivilivinzi village. There is history that two of these cattle were purchased from Masikili village (where there is also suspicious cases) in June 2013.
Clinical signs suggestive of foot and mouth disease. Twenty-four cattle have mouth lesions (salivation and ulcers).
9 cattle from three kraals with a total herd of 470 heads have oral and foot lesions suggestive of foot and mouth disease.
20 cattle out of 70 in Kavango East Region with lesions suggestive of FMD.
14 cattle out of a population of 2,458 were found to have oral and hoof lesions suspected to be of foot and mouth disease.
36 cattle from 4 different kraals at Shaile-Kweha Island were found to have lesions suspected of foot and mouth disease. The total cattle population of the village is 849.

Three out of a population of 604 were found to have lesions suspected of foot and mouth disease. The cattle are salivating and have blisters and ulcers on tongues, dental pads and inter-digital spaces.

Cattle showing signs consistent with FMD (inter-digital ulcers, coronary band ulcers, ulcers on tongue, ulcers on dental pads) within the vicinity of the kraal that tested positive to FMD. The ulcers are mainly in early healing stage and late healing stage.
